rationale: Round 0 built and ran correctly, so this candidate pushes obfuscation intensity up while protecting the program's dominant cost: nestedloop's six-deep hot loop in a very small binary (3 functions, 231 text bytes), where per-iteration overhead is multiplied heavily. FLA gets the highest SecurityGain/DiversityGain because control-flow flattening gives the strongest structural resistance against recovery of the nested-loop logic, with a moderate RuntimeCost weight so it is not preferentially steered onto the hottest loop body; BCF keeps solid security weight but the lowest RuntimeCost weight since bogus-arithmetic predicates on a hot inner loop would be the single worst slowdown-per-benefit trade here. SUB, SPLIT, and IBR are cheap, correctness-safe transforms and so carry high RuntimeCost weights (allowed even on hot code) with solid security/diversity weights, giving broad instruction-level and branch-level divergence at minimal overhead. ICALL and IGV round out diversity against static call-graph and global-data analysis at mid weights, since this binary has little global state and few call sites, making them lower-yield. CorrectnessRisk weights are kept low across the board given the prior round showed clean compilation and execution, leaving headroom to escalate further if this round also passes.
